Giwa, who is standing trial over allegations that he forged the letterhead of a Senior Advocate of Nigeria, Chief Awa Kalu, SAN, appeared before the High Court of the Federal Capital Territory to defend himself.
The police had accused Giwa of forging Kalu’s letterhead, but the senior lawyer had reportedly distanced himself from the allegation in a letter to the Inspector-General of Police, Kayode Egbetokun.
In the letter dated May 30, 2025, Kalu clarified that he neither lodged a complaint with the police nor reported Giwa for allegedly forging his law firm’s letterhead. He also stated that his letterhead had not been forged.
Despite the clarification, the police proceeded with the prosecution of Giwa. At the resumed hearing, Dr Sonny Ajala, SAN, counsel to Kalu, who was subpoenaed as a non-party witness, moved an application seeking to set aside the subpoena requiring the senior lawyer to appear before the court.
However, the prosecutor, S.A. Medugu, applied for a warrant of arrest to be issued against Kalu.
Giwa, who appeared in person as the first defendant, opposed the hearing of the application and further proceedings, citing a petition he had submitted against the trial judge over alleged bias and partiality.
He told the court that he had written to the Chief Judge of the FCT on November 3, requesting an investigation into what he described as bias by the trial court and the alleged disclosure of his private information to one of the complainants.
Giwa further alleged that the court had acted partially and that he could not obtain justice before it.
He also claimed that after the court requested his wife’s telephone number, she began receiving threatening messages.
Supporting Giwa’s position, Ajala urged the court to remit the case file to the Chief Judge of the FCT for consideration, citing the weight of the allegations raised against the trial judge.
However, Justice Onwuegbuzie ruled that the court had not received any response to Giwa’s letter seeking the judge’s recusal and ordered that proceedings in the case should continue.
The court subsequently adjourned the matter until December 2 for ruling on Kalu’s application seeking to set aside the subpoena.
